title: Changing an Orbit event payload in packages/events requires bumping schemaVersion and registering it in the registry
body: Consumers built on `packages/events` validate every message against `events/registry.ts` and reject unknown versions, so a payload change without a new `schemaVersion` sends every message to the dead-letter queue. Add the new version with `defineEvent('order.created', 3, schema)`, keep the old version registered until all consumers are deployed, and run `make events-check`, which the CI job `events-compat` also runs.

title: Replay Orbit dead-lettered RabbitMQ messages with orbit-cli events replay, not by moving them in the management UI
body: Moving messages from `billing-events.dlq` back with the RabbitMQ management UI or a shovel drops the `x-tenant-id` and `x-event-version` headers, so consumers fail again or process them under no tenant. Use `orbit-cli events replay --queue billing-events.dlq --since 2h --env staging`, which republishes through `packages/events` with headers intact; add `--dry-run` first to see the count.

title: Orbit billing events must use a stable event_id derived from the order, otherwise retries charge customers twice
body: The `billing` consumer deduplicates on `event_id` in the `billing.processed_events` table. In the 2025-06 double-charge incident `api` generated a fresh `uuid4()` on every publish retry, so each retry looked like a new charge. Build the id with `billingEventId(orderId, 'charge')` from `packages/events`, which is deterministic, and never generate it inside a retry loop.

title: Orbit preview environments receive no payment provider webhooks; set BILLING_FAKE_PSP=1 to test checkout there
body: Stripe test-mode webhooks are only routed to staging through the `stripe-relay` service, so in a `pr-<number>` namespace orders stay in `pending_payment` forever and `billing.settled` never fires. Preview deployments should set `BILLING_FAKE_PSP=1` in `deploy/preview/values.yaml`, which makes `billing` settle payments immediately; use staging when you need real webhook behaviour.

title: Orbit make test uses a separate throwaway Postgres on port 5434 that make dev does not start
body: The test suite connects to the `orbit_test` database on host port 5434, a tmpfs-backed container started by `make test-db-up`, so running `make dev` alone leaves pytest failing with 'connection refused' on 5434. Run `make test-db-up` once per session (or `make test`, which starts it if missing) and never point `TEST_DATABASE_URL` at the dev database on 5433, because the fixtures truncate every table.

title: Orbit data backfills go in services/core/backfills and run with make backfill, never inside an alembic migration
body: The migration job in the deploy pipeline has a 10 minute timeout; in the 2025-01 release a backfill inside a migration updated 40M rows, hit the timeout and left the deploy half-applied. Keep migrations schema-only and put data changes in `services/core/backfills/<date>_<name>.py`, then run `make backfill NAME=<name> ENV=staging` (batched, resumable via the `backfill_progress` table) after the deploy.

title: Orbit alembic migrations must create indexes on large tables CONCURRENTLY inside an autocommit block to pass migration-lint
body: The `migration-lint` CI job runs squawk on the generated SQL and fails on a plain `CREATE INDEX` against tables listed in `services/core/migrations/large_tables.txt`, because it locks writes during the build. Use `op.create_index(..., postgresql_concurrently=True)` wrapped in `with op.get_context().autocommit_block():`, since CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside alembic's transaction.

title: Orbit v2 list endpoints must use cursor pagination via paginate_cursor; offset and page params are rejected
body: Offset pagination on large tenants caused slow `OFFSET` scans and duplicated rows while data changed, so every v2 list route uses `paginate_cursor()` from `api/src/lib/pagination` with `?cursor=` and `?limit=` (max 200). The `api-v2-lint` check fails on any `offset` or `page` query parameter in `api/src/routes/v2`, and the response must return `next_cursor`.

title: Orbit scheduled reports must use the tenant's timezone from tenants.tz, because Celery beat schedules in UTC
body: Celery beat runs in UTC, so a daily report computed with `date.today()` cuts the day at midnight UTC and tenants in America or Asia see yesterday's orders missing or duplicated. Load the zone stored in the `tenants.tz` column and compute boundaries with `tenant_day_bounds(tenant, day)` from `orbit_core.time`; never call `datetime.now()` without the tenant zone in `reports` code.

title: Orbit Celery beat must run as a single replica in worker-beat; scaling it sends scheduled jobs twice
body: Beat has no leader election, so each replica fires every schedule. In 2025-02 someone scaled `worker-beat` to 2 replicas during an autoscaling change and every tenant received duplicate invoice reminder emails. Keep `replicas: 1` and `strategy: Recreate` in `deploy/charts/worker-beat/values.yaml`; scale the `worker` and `worker-slow` deployments instead.

title: Orbit Redis cache keys must be built with cache_key(tenant_id, ...) so cached data is not shared across tenants
body: Raw keys like `product:42` collided between tenants and served one tenant's catalog to another, because the cache is consulted before `TenantScopedSession` ever runs. Use `cache_key(tenant_id, 'product', 42)` from `orbit_core.cache`, which prefixes `t:<tenant>:`. To clear one tenant run `make cache-flush TENANT=<id> ENV=staging`, which deletes with SCAN on that prefix instead of KEYS.

title: Orbit web app environment variables only reach the browser bundle if prefixed ORBIT_PUBLIC_
body: `apps/web/vite.config.ts` sets `envPrefix: 'ORBIT_PUBLIC_'`, so a variable named `API_BASE_URL` is undefined in the browser even though it is set in the deployment. Rename it `ORBIT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` and read it via `import.meta.env`. Never give a secret this prefix: everything with it is inlined into the public JS, and the `bundle-secrets-scan` CI step fails on values that match Vault paths.

title: Orbit PRs touching apps/web components are blocked until the Chromatic ui-review check is accepted
body: Every component in `packages/ui` and `apps/web/src/components` has Storybook stories that Chromatic snapshots; any visual diff turns the `ui-review` status check yellow and blocks merge. Open the Chromatic link from the check, accept the intended changes, and the status goes green. Run `pnpm --filter web storybook` locally to check stories before pushing.

title: Every Orbit Prometheus alert needs a runbook_url annotation pointing to docs/runbooks, or alert-lint fails
body: On-call for Orbit is the PagerDuty schedule `orbit-primary`, paged from rules in `deploy/monitoring/alerts/*.yaml`. The `alert-lint` CI job rejects any alert without `annotations.runbook_url` pointing to an existing `docs/runbooks/<alert-name>.md`. Write the runbook in the same PR as the alert, including the first three diagnostic commands to run.

title: Orbit Python services must log through orbit_core.log.get_logger and never put emails or names in log fields
body: Logs are shipped as JSON to Loki and retained 90 days, so PII in logs is a GDPR problem. Use `log = get_logger(__name__)` from `orbit_core.log` (structlog with tenant and request ids bound automatically) instead of `logging.getLogger`. The `pii-scan` CI job fails on log calls with keys such as `email=`, `name=` or `phone=`; log `user_id` instead.

title: Orbit reports pods stay Pending unless they carry the workload=reports toleration for the reports-pool nodes
body: The `reports` service and `worker-slow` run on the dedicated high-memory node pool `reports-pool`, which is tainted `workload=reports:NoSchedule`. A chart copied from another service without the toleration and the `nodeSelector: pool: reports-pool` stays Pending with 'untolerated taint'. Use the `orbit.reportsScheduling` helper from `deploy/charts/_lib` instead of writing them by hand.

title: Build Orbit service images with make image SERVICE=<name>; plain docker build cannot reach the internal pip index
body: Internal packages such as `orbit-core` and the patched pyarrow wheel come from the private index in `ORBIT_PIP_INDEX`, passed as a BuildKit secret mount. A plain `docker build .` has no secret and fails with 'no matching distribution found for orbit-core'. Run `make image SERVICE=core`, which calls `docker buildx build --secret id=pipindex` and reuses the cache at `ghcr.io/orbit/build-cache`.

title: Orbit staging enforces 100 requests per minute per token; load tests must use the loadtest token from Vault
body: The `api` rate limiter is backed by Redis and disabled locally unless `RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=1`, which is why load scripts pass on a laptop and get HTTP 429 on staging. For k6 runs against staging, read the token from Vault at `secret/orbit/api/staging/loadtest_token` and send it as `X-Orbit-Loadtest`, which raises the limit to 5000 per minute; announce the run in `#orbit-staging` first.

title: Orbit local emails go to Mailpit on localhost:8025 and staging only delivers to allowlisted domains
body: `make dev` runs Mailpit, so transactional emails are visible at http://localhost:8025 and never leave the machine. On staging the `notifications` worker only sends to domains in `EMAIL_ALLOWLIST_DOMAINS` (default `orbit.dev`) and silently drops the rest with an `email.suppressed` log line, which is why a test with a personal Gmail address shows nothing. Use a `+alias@orbit.dev` address.

title: After changing Orbit search mappings run make search-reindex, which builds a new index and swaps the orbit-search alias
body: OpenSearch cannot change the type of an existing field, so editing `services/core/search/mappings.py` and deploying leaves the old mapping in place. `make search-reindex ENV=staging` creates `orbit-search-v<N+1>`, reindexes from Postgres and atomically moves the `orbit-search` alias. The nightly staging DB restore does not touch OpenSearch; the `search-reindex` CronJob at 04:00 UTC resyncs it, so staging search may show deleted records until then.

title: Ledgerline stores amounts as BIGINT minor units with a currency; use Money.ofMinor and never divide by 100
body: Currencies have different exponents: JPY has 0 decimals and KWD has 3. In the 2025-09 incident a payout job divided by 100 and sent JPY payouts 100 times too large. Always convert with `Money.ofMinor(amount, currency)` and `money.toMajorString()` from the internal `ll-money` library, which reads exponents from ISO 4217, and keep the `amount_minor` and `currency` columns together in every table.

title: Ledgerline journal entries must be written through LedgerWriter.post; direct inserts into ledger.entries fail the balance trigger
body: The ledger is double-entry: every journal's debits must equal its credits per currency. The deferred constraint trigger `trg_entries_balanced` on `ledger.entries` raises 'journal not balanced' at commit if you insert rows by hand, including in test fixtures. Build a `Journal` and call `LedgerWriter.post(journal)` in `ledger-core`; for fixtures use `JournalFixtures.transfer(from, to, money)`.

title: Ledgerline Kafka consumers must deduplicate through the inbox_messages table because delivery is at-least-once
body: Consumer rebalances in `ledger-core` redeliver already processed records, and a redelivered `ll.payments.captured.v2` once posted the same capture twice. Wrap handlers with `InboxGuard.handle(record) { ... }`, which inserts `(topic, message_id)` into `ledger.inbox_messages` in the same transaction as the business write and skips duplicates. Never rely on committing offsets for exactly-once.

title: Ledgerline services must never publish to Kafka inside a DB transaction; write to outbox_events and let outbox-relay publish
body: In the 2025-05 phantom payout incident `payments-gateway` published `payout.requested` and then its transaction rolled back, so the bank received payouts that did not exist in the ledger. Insert the event into the service's `outbox_events` table in the same transaction with `Outbox.enqueue(event)`; the `outbox-relay` deployment polls it and publishes to Kafka in order. The `no-kafka-in-tx` ArchUnit test fails on a `KafkaTemplate` call inside `@Transactional`.

title: Ledgerline Kafka topics must be declared in infra/kafka/topics.tf; auto-create works locally but not in uat or prod
body: The local docker compose broker has `auto.create.topics.enable=true`, so a new topic appears on first produce and everything works on a laptop, then fails in uat with 'UNKNOWN_TOPIC_OR_PARTITION'. Topics follow the name `ll.<domain>.<event>.v<N>` and are created by adding a `ll_topic` module block in `infra/kafka/topics.tf` with partitions and retention, applied by the `infra-kafka` pipeline.

title: Ledgerline balance events must be keyed by account_id, not payment_id, so updates to one account stay ordered
body: Kafka only orders records within a partition. When `ll.ledger.balance-changed.v1` was keyed by `payment_id`, a debit and a refund on the same account landed on different partitions, were applied out of order and briefly showed a negative balance that triggered `risk-engine` blocks (2025-04). Produce with `key = accountId.toString()`; the `topic-key-check` test in `ledger-core` asserts the key for each topic.

title: Ledgerline settlement-batch runs at 22:30 Europe/London, not UTC, and skips UK bank holidays from a yearly calendar file
body: The `settlement-batch` CronJob uses `timeZone: Europe/London`, so in summer it fires at 21:30 UTC; payments captured after the cutoff settle the next business day. Business days come from `calendars/uk-bank-holidays.yaml`, which must be updated every December or the batch runs on a holiday and the bank rejects the file. Check the next run with `llctl settlement next-run --env uat`.

title: Always pass --env to Ledgerline llctl commands; it silently reuses the last context, and prod needs llctl auth elevate
body: `llctl` stores the last used environment in `~/.llctl/context`, so a command you meant for `uat` runs against `prod-eu` if that was your last session. Always pass `--env uat` explicitly. Write commands in `prod-eu` or `prod-us` additionally require `llctl auth elevate --reason <ticket>`, which issues a 30 minute token and posts to `#ll-prod-access`.

title: Ledgerline local Kafka is reachable on localhost:29092 from the host but kafka:9092 from other containers
body: `make up` starts the compose stack with two advertised listeners: `PLAINTEXT_HOST://localhost:29092` for apps run from the IDE and `PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092` inside the compose network. Using 9092 from the host connects, then fails on metadata with 'Connection to node 1 (kafka:9092) could not be established'. Local Postgres is on `localhost:55432`; both are already set in `.env.local.example`.

title: Only Ledgerline vault-tokenizer may handle card PANs; other services work with tok_ tokens and the pci-boundary test enforces it
body: Card numbers exist only inside `vault-tokenizer` in the `pci` Kubernetes namespace, which is the only component in PCI DSS scope. Every other service receives `tok_...` tokens; adding a `pan`, `cardNumber` or `cvv` field to a DTO outside `pci/` fails the `pci-boundary` ArchUnit test, and the log pipeline drops lines matching a Luhn-valid number. Call `TokenizerClient.detokenizeForPsp()` only from `payments-gateway`'s PSP adapters.

title: Ledgerline sandbox payments go to psp-sim, where magic amounts trigger declines, timeouts and chargebacks
body: In `sandbox` and local `make up`, `payments-gateway` talks to the `psp-sim` simulator instead of a real PSP. Amounts in minor units select the outcome: `40400` declines with `insufficient_funds`, `50400` times out after 35 seconds, `60100` succeeds and then sends a chargeback webhook after 2 minutes; any other amount succeeds. The full table is in `tools/psp-sim/README.md`.

title: Ledgerline Flyway migrations use timestamp versions V<yyyyMMddHHmm>__desc.sql and applied files must never be edited
body: Sequential versions like `V42__` collided between parallel branches, so migrations in `ledger-core/src/main/resources/db/migration` are named `V202510061430__add_payout_status.sql`. Editing an already applied file changes its checksum and the service refuses to start with 'Validate failed: Migration checksum mismatch'. Write a new migration instead; `./gradlew flywayRepair` is only run by the DBA on-call.

title: Ledgerline migrations touching ledger.entries must start with SET lock_timeout = '3s' to avoid blocking payments
body: In the 2025-07 incident an `ALTER TABLE ledger.entries ADD COLUMN` waited behind a long reporting query, and every payment write queued behind the ALTER for four minutes. Start such migrations with `SET lock_timeout = '3s';` so they fail fast and the deploy retries, and add an `-- ll:online` header comment. The `migration-guard` CI step rejects migrations on hot tables listed in `db/hot_tables.txt` without both.

title: Ledgerline feature flags are in Unleash and change at runtime; kill_ flags must default to fail-closed
body: Ledgerline flags live in Unleash at `https://flags.ledgerline.internal` and the SDK polls every 10 seconds, so a toggle takes effect without a deploy. Flags prefixed `kill_` (for example `kill_payouts_sepa`) are kill switches: read them with `Flags.killSwitch("kill_payouts_sepa")`, which returns true (feature off) when Unleash is unreachable. Ordinary flags use `Flags.isOn(name, context)` and default to off.

title: Ledgerline pact-verify fails until the consumer contract is published with make pact-publish
body: `payments-gateway` and `ledger-core` share Pact contracts through the broker at `pact.ledgerline.internal`. When a consumer changes an interaction, the provider's Buildkite step `pact-verify` fails with 'no pact found for consumer version' until the consumer branch runs `make pact-publish`. Publish from the consumer first, then rebuild the provider; `can-i-deploy` gates the uat deploy on both.

title: Ledgerline Kotlin services need JDK 21; a Gradle daemon started on JDK 17 fails with invalid source release 21
body: The Gradle builds in `ledger-core`, `payments-gateway` and `settlement-batch` set `jvmToolchain(21)`, but the IDE or shell may start the daemon with an older JDK. Run `sdk env` in the repo root (reads `.sdkmanrc`), then `./gradlew --stop` to kill the stale daemon. In IntelliJ set Gradle JVM to the project SDK; CI uses the `ll-jdk21` Buildkite agent queue.

title: Ledgerline Go services need GOPRIVATE=git.ledgerline.internal/* to download the internal ledgerkit module
body: `fx-rates` and `recon-worker` import `git.ledgerline.internal/platform/ledgerkit`. Without `GOPRIVATE`, `go mod download` asks proxy.golang.org and fails with '410 Gone' or 'unrecognized import path'. Run `go env -w GOPRIVATE=git.ledgerline.internal/*` and add a `~/.netrc` entry with a GitLab token that has `read_api`; `make go-setup` does both.

title: Ledgerline payments-gateway rejects FX conversions with FX_RATE_STALE when the cached rate is older than 26 hours
body: `fx-rates` pulls ECB reference rates once a day at 16:15 CET, and `payments-gateway` refuses cross-currency payments when the rate is older than `FX_MAX_AGE` (26h). The ECB publishes nothing on weekends and TARGET holidays, so `FX_MAX_AGE_WEEKEND=74h` applies from Friday 16:15; if conversions fail on a weekday, check the `fx-rates-pull` job logs with `llctl jobs logs fx-rates-pull --env prod-eu` before raising the limit.

title: Reprocess a Ledgerline bank reconciliation file with llctl recon reingest; re-uploading it to SFTP is skipped as a duplicate
body: `recon-worker` picks up CAMT.053 statements from `/inbound/<bank>` on the SFTP host and records each file's SHA-256 in `recon.ingested_files`, so uploading the same file again is ignored with 'duplicate statement'. After fixing a parser bug run `llctl recon reingest --file-id <id> --env uat`, which clears the previous matches for that file and parses it again.

title: Ledgerline on-call: any payout failure lasting over 5 minutes is SEV1, declared with /incident declare in #ll-incidents
body: The primary rotation is the Opsgenie schedule `ll-payments-primary`, with handoff every Monday at 10:00 Europe/London. Payout failures longer than 5 minutes, ledger imbalance alerts and PCI zone alerts are always SEV1: run `/incident declare sev1` in `#ll-incidents`, which opens the bridge and pages the secondary and the duty manager. Postmortems are due within 5 business days in `docs/postmortems/`.

title: Ledgerline kubectl edits are reverted by Argo CD self-heal; change manifests in the ll-gitops repo instead
body: All Ledgerline namespaces are managed by Argo CD with `selfHeal: true`, so `kubectl edit` or `kubectl scale` on a deployment is undone within about three minutes. Change `ll-gitops/apps/<service>/overlays/<env>/` and merge; for an emergency scale during an incident, run `llctl argo pause <service> --env prod-eu` first and record it in the incident channel.

title: Ledgerline secrets are SOPS-encrypted in ll-gitops/secrets; decrypt locally with make secrets-decrypt using the env reader role
body: Secrets are not in a vault server: they live as `ll-gitops/secrets/<env>/<service>.enc.yaml`, encrypted with a per-environment AWS KMS key. To read them for local runs, assume the `ll-<env>-secrets-readers` role and run `make secrets-decrypt ENV=uat SERVICE=payments-gateway`, which writes a git-ignored `.env.secrets`; editing needs the `ll-<env>-secrets-editors` role and `sops <file>`. Never commit a decrypted file; the `sops-guard` pre-commit hook blocks it.

title: Ledgerline balance reads after a write must use the primary; the ledger-ro replica can lag up to 30 seconds
body: Methods annotated `@ReadOnlyReplica` route to the `ledger-ro` Postgres replica, which is fine for reports but lags up to 30 seconds under batch load. In 2025-08 a payout check read a stale balance from the replica right after a debit and allowed an overdraft. Read balances you are about to act on with `BalanceService.currentFromPrimary(accountId)` and keep `@ReadOnlyReplica` for dashboards and exports.

title: Ledgerline uat data is refreshed from masked prod every Sunday at 02:00 UTC; keep test merchants in fixtures/uat-merchants.json
body: The `uat-refresh` job replaces the uat Postgres databases and Kafka consumer offsets with a masked prod copy every Sunday at 02:00 UTC, so merchants, API keys and accounts created by hand during the week disappear. Add persistent merchants to `fixtures/uat-merchants.json`, which the `uat-seed` job loads after each refresh, and regenerate their API keys with `llctl merchants rotate-key --env uat`.

title: Ledgerline POST /v3/payments requires an Idempotency-Key header; reusing a key with a different body returns 422
body: `payments-gateway` stores each key with a hash of the request body in `api.idempotency_keys` for 24 hours. A retry with the same key and body returns the original response, but the same key with a different amount or currency returns `422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`, and a missing header returns `400`. Client SDKs must generate one key per logical payment and reuse it only across retries of that exact request.
